content: Clarithromycin can increase its own levels or effects by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored in such cases. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of duvelisib by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution is advised, and monitoring is necessary. Clarithromycin elevates the levels or effects of efavirenz by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Clarithromycin raises the levels or effects of elagolix by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be adjusted or closely monitored. Co-administration of elagolix 200 mg BID with strong CYP3A inhibitors for more than one month is not recommended. Elagolix decreases the levels or effects of clarithromycin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be adjusted or closely monitored. Elagolix is a weak-to-moderate CYP3A4 inducer, and CYP3A substrates should be monitored if co-administered. Dose adjustments of CYP3A substrates may be necessary. Clarithromycin increases the levels of elvitegravir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Elvitegravir is a CYP3A4 substrate, and co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may elevate its levels. Clarithromycin and cobicistat can mutually increase each other's levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. If creatinine clearance (CrCl) is less than 60 mL/min, the clarithromycin dose should be reduced by 50%. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of encorafenib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Encorafenib both inhibits and induces CYP3A4 at clinically relevant plasma concentrations, potentially leading to increased toxicity or reduced efficacy of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates. Clarithromycin enhances the toxicity of enfortumab vedotin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. Enfortumab vedotin releases monomethyl auristatin E (MMAE) via proteolytic cleavage, and MMAE is primarily metabolized by CYP3A4. Co-administration with dual P-gp and strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase MMAE exposure, raising the risk of enfortumab vedotin toxicities. Close monitoring for toxicity signs is essential. Enzalutamide reduces the levels or effects of clarithromycin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of eplerenone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Clarithromycin elevates the levels or effects of erlotinib by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of erythromycin base by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and erythromycin base reciprocally increases clarithromycin levels. Caution and monitoring are required. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate, lactobionate, and stearate all increase clarithromycin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Clarithromycin decreases the levels or effects of estradiol by altering intestinal flora, which applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low. However, clarithromycin can also increase estradiol levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of estradiol vaginal forms by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may elevate plasma concentrations of estrogens and their associated toxicities. Clarithromycin decreases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by altering intestinal flora, which applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low. However, clarithromycin can also increase their levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Clarithromycin decreases the levels or effects of estropipate by altering intestinal flora, which applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low. However, clarithromycin can also increase estropipate levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Clarithromycin increases eszopiclone levels by enhancing gastrointestinal absorption, which applies only to oral forms of both agents. It also elevates eszopiclone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be adjusted or closely monitored, and the eszopiclone starting dose should be reduced to 1 mg/day. Clarithromycin decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora, which applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of etoposide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Clarithromycin elevates the levels or effects of eucalyptus by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Clarithromycin and ezogabine both increase QTc interval prolongation. Caution and monitoring are required. Ezogabine has been associated with slight and transient QT prolongation, particularly at doses titrated to 1200 mg/day. QT interval monitoring is recommended when ezogabine is prescribed with agents known to prolong the QT interval. Fedratinib increases clarithromycin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Dose adjustments of CYP3A4 substrates may be required. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of felodipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Enhanced effects of calcium channel blockers may lead to hypotension, edema, bradycardia, and acute kidney injury due to reduced renal blood flow. Clarithromycin elevates the levels or effects of finasteride by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Clarithromycin and flecainide both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of fludrocortisone by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Clarithromycin and fluoxetine both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of flurazepam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Clarithromycin elevates the levels or effects of fluticasone furoate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic exposure to fluticasone. Clarithromycin and fluticasone inhaled forms interact similarly, requiring caution and monitoring. Clarithromycin and fluvoxamine both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Clarithromycin and foscarnet both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Clarithromycin increases fostamatinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase exposure to R406 (the major active metabolite of fostamatinib). Monitoring for toxicities that may require dose reduction is essential. Clarithromycin increases gefitinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase the risk of gefitinib adverse effects. Clarithromycin and gemtuzumab both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Clarithromycin increases gentamicin levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. Clarithromycin and gepirone both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Clarithromycin increases glimepiride, glipizide, and glyburide levels by competing for plasma protein binding. Caution and monitoring are required due to the risk of hypoglycemia. Goserelin increases clarithromycin toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary, as this increases the risk of torsades de pointes. Clarithromycin elevates guanfacine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors significantly increase guanfacine plasma concentrations. For extended-release guanfacine, the dosage should be halved if co-administered. Specific recommendations for immediate-release guanfacine are unavailable. Histrelin increases clarithromycin toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary, as this increases the risk of torsades de pointes. Clarithromycin increases hydrocodone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may elevate hydrocodone plasma concentrations, potentially leading to fatal respiratory depression. Clarithromycin increases hydrocortisone levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. Hydroxyzine increases clarithromycin toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary, as this increases the risk of torsades de pointes. Clarithromycin decreases ifosfamide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may reduce the metabolism of ifosfamide to its active alkylating metabolites, decreasing its efficacy. Clarithromycin and iloperidone both prolong the QTc interval. Iloperidone increases clarithromycin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Iloperidone is a time-dependent CYP3A inhibitor and may elevate plasma levels of drugs predominantly eliminated by CYP3A4. Clarithromycin increases imatinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are required. Clarithromycin increases indacaterol levels by modulating P-gp and CYP3A4 activities. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Indacaterol and clarithromycin both prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of ventricular arrhythmias. Clarithromycin elevates indinavir levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised.
